source_neutral.procedure: Examine the surviving draft as discrete units: leaves, gatherings, inserted slips, chapter bundles, and recopied or typed sections. Each unit is treated as having passed through two phases: compositional handling by the author and any copyist, typist or editor, including first drafting, revision campaigns, renumbering, relocation, recopying and assembly; and post-compositional handling by heirs, dealers, collectors, archivists and conservators, including sorting, foliation, binding, rehousing, removal and interfiling. Reconstruct handling backward from the present archival state to the author's last handling, then forward through compositional events, maintaining separate event records for the two phases. Before starting, establish how many witnesses survive, whether the draft is manuscript, typescript or mixed, whether more than one hand is present, and whether accession or provenance files exist; the packet does not supply these facts.
source_neutral.action: Inventory every unit in its present order and assign a neutral identifier independent of narrative order and existing numbering. For each unit, create an event record with one entry per event, specifying event type, responsible party, time, purpose and supporting evidence. Event types include drafting, revision, renumbering, relocation, recopying, assembly, foliation, binding, conservation and transfer of ownership. Identify the responsible hand or agent, or enter 'unidentified'; express time as a date or a relative interval such as 'after event X, before event Y'. Tag each entry as 'contemporaneous record' or 'reconstructed from trace'. Contemporaneous records include dated leaves, dated correspondence, accession registers, sale catalogues and conservation reports. Traces include superseded page numbers, ink or pencil layers, paper stock, watermarks, pinholes, stubs, offsets, text running across a leaf boundary, and deletion and insertion patterns. Keep compositional and post-compositional records separate. Inspect every transition to determine whether each state of a unit has an accounted-for predecessor and whether party, time and purpose agree across units sharing an event, such as a renumbering campaign. Mark every unexplained transition as an open break and draft each assembly sequence compatible with the event records. Log each observation against its unit and transition, with its record-type tag.
source_neutral.observables: Signals of continuity are superseded numbering that resolves into a coherent earlier sequence; uninterrupted text across leaves placed adjacent by the event records; paper stock, ink and hand consistent within a campaign and with its date interval; correspondence or dated leaves agreeing with the relative order; and archival records accounting for present foliation, binding and order. Signals of an unexplained transition are a unit without a predecessor state or a record of entry into the collection; numbering sequences that cannot both hold; a change of paper or ink in mid-passage without a recorded event; text continuing between leaves that are not currently adjacent; foliation in a non-authorial hand conflicting with authorial pagination; stubs or numbering gaps indicating removed leaves; a dated letter conflicting with a unit's placement; and two event entries assigning incompatible times or parties to one event.
source_neutral.inferential_warrant: Continuity in the post-compositional event record supports the claim that the examined arrangement is the arrangement the author left, allowing its order to serve as evidence of authorial assembly. Continuity in a unit's compositional event record supports the proposed sequence of drafting, revision and placement for that unit. Grade claims as supported by contemporaneous record, supported by reconstruction from trace, or unsupported across an unexplained transition. Select as the best explanation the sequence leaving the fewest unexplained transitions and contradictions, and report each step's grade. An unexplained transition weakens the claims dependent on that transition; competing assembly sequences at that point remain retained. Present order and narrative order are not treated as composition order unless the event record independently links them.
source_neutral.problem_decomposition: The analysis relates discrete physical and textual units, their successive states, the events connecting those states, the parties responsible, time intervals, purposes and evidence. Shared events connect records across units and require agreement about party, time and purpose. Separate compositional changes from subsequent handling while examining how both contributed to the surviving arrangement. Account for a recopied or replacement leaf occupying an earlier leaf's position; later revision layers or non-authorial markings; leaves from another draft or work interfiled with the draft; and ordering imposed after the author. Distinguish the question of whether the present arrangement matches what the author left from the reconstruction of drafting, revision and assembly within that arrangement. Authorial alteration is an object of investigation; post-compositional or non-authorial changes constitute the changes to be distinguished from it, and that distinction may remain uncertain.
source_neutral.next_inquiry: For each open break, collate further witnesses, request accession and conservation files, consult dated correspondence, and re-inspect the material features at that transition.
source_neutral.limits: Stop when every transition of every unit has been classified as documented, reconstructed with a stated basis, or an open break, and the accessible witnesses and records have been consulted. A complete event record does not establish that its entries are true: authorial dates may be retrospective or mistaken, letters may misreport progress, and archival files may omit resorting or refoliation. Unrecorded alteration remains possible, including discarded or recopied leaves whose earlier layers left no trace. An unexplained transition or missing record does not establish interference, loss or reordering. Inferential strength depends on recording reliability. Most compositional entries are reconstructed afterward from traces rather than recorded at the time of handling by a responsible party; those reconstructions depend on interpretations of the same features they are used to order. Distinguishing authorial alteration from post-compositional or non-authorial change is itself uncertain. Continuity of documented handling bears on identity and handling history, but does not establish information about witnesses that never entered the record. A local mark or reading does not establish a whole composition history. This is a proposed procedure, and no observations have been made. The accompanying practitioner description is an authored hypothesis rather than verified consensus.
